headline: Deload: over target on paper, but the pounding stayed low
narrative: A deload has one job — come in under the number — and this week didn't quite manage it. Vert finished a fair way over the reduced target, with time on feet a touch over its small ask too. The honest read is gentler than the percentage suggests: almost all the climbing came from ascent-only machine work on the steep treadmill and stair machine, with barely a metre of real descent all week, so the legs took far less pounding than the headline implies. The running stayed short and easy — a club run, a hilly parkrun, some flat miles. Still, on the next deload, under means under.

The real work happened in the gym. Physio started Monday and rehab strength sessions stacked up around a new programme hitting the quads, adductors and hamstrings — exactly where the watch sits. With no descending to provoke it, the right quad stayed silent, which makes next week's return to full Build volume the proper test. Week thirteen also opens two new fronts: night-running practice begins and a fuelling rehearsal is due. The cumulative push toward Costa Blanca remains on schedule; arrive at next week rested and this overshoot is forgiven.
